Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray reveals a large, dense opacity in the left upper lung zone with an irregular, somewhat linear appearance suggestive of a retained foreign body (such as wood, which can be radiopaque or mimic consolidation), combined with blunting of the costophrenic angle indicating hemothorax/pleural effusion; this specific pattern in a trauma patient is characteristic of a penetrating injury by a wooden object.
